funFacts: It's the smallest planet in the solar system.
A single day on Mercury (sunrise to sunrise) lasts 176 Earth days — longer than its own year.
It has almost no atmosphere, so its temperature swings wildly between day and night.
mercury.passiveDescription: Never takes damage from the yellow Sun's flares.
mercury.activeDescription: +250% speed and slows nearby asteroids. A teammate near you gets the same slowing field.

funFacts: It's the hottest planet in the solar system (over 460°C / 860°F), even hotter than Mercury, due to an extreme greenhouse effect.
It spins backwards compared to most planets.
A day on Venus lasts longer than its own year.
venus.passiveDescription: Small asteroids that get close turn red, as if burning up, and crumble into dust on contact — they never hurt her.
venus.activeDescription: Total temporary invulnerability. A teammate near you gets the same shield.

earth.orbitalPeriod: 1 Earth year (365 days) — the reference point
funFacts: It's the only known planet with life.
71% of its surface is covered in water.
It has a single natural satellite: the Moon.
earth.passiveDescription: Its magnetosphere always protects it from the yellow Sun's flares (never the Red Sun) — every blocked hit triggers an aurora at the point of impact.
earth.activeDescription: Its moon spins 15x faster and destroys any asteroid it touches. A teammate near you also disintegrates nearby asteroids.

funFacts: It has the largest volcano in the solar system: Olympus Mons.
It's known as the "Red Planet" because of the iron oxide on its surface.
It has two small moons: Phobos and Deimos.
mars.activeDescription: Disintegrates nearby asteroids in every direction. A teammate near you also disintegrates asteroids around them.

funFacts: It's the largest planet in the solar system — over 1,300 Earths could fit inside it.
Its Great Red Spot is a storm bigger than Earth that's been raging for centuries.
It has over 90 known moons.
jupiter.passiveDescription: Larger size, small asteroids disintegrate on contact without hurting it, and it only takes damage every 2 flares.
jupiter.activeDescription: Self invulnerability. In a team, it also protects and heals (+3 lives) the first teammate who gets close, and Jupiter earns +3 stars for helping.

funFacts: It's famous for its spectacular rings made of ice and rock.
It's less dense than water — it would theoretically float in a giant bathtub.
It has over 140 known moons, including Titan, larger than Mercury.
saturn.passiveDescription: Increases the odds of healing pulsars appearing (+30% solo). In a team, EVERY player in the room gets the bonus — double the pulsars for everyone.
saturn.activeDescription: Repels nearby asteroids and is the only planet with defense against the Red Sun's flares. A teammate near you gets the same repel and defense.

funFacts: It has the fastest winds in the solar system: up to 2,100 km/h (1,300 mph).
It was the first planet discovered through math before it was ever directly observed.
Since its discovery in 1846, it completed its first full orbit of the Sun in 2011.
neptune.passiveDescription: Slightly slows down any asteroid that gets very close to you, at no cost. Only protects you.
neptune.activeDescription: Nearly freezes nearby asteroids solid and destroys them if they touch you. The storm is felt across the WHOLE room — every teammate, no matter the distance, gets a lighter version of the freeze while it lasts.
